item.title: -1 then +1 so technically +2
item.content:encoded:
Currently, the only known way of preventing SCP-001-J-EX-D-ARC-1 instances from viewing documentation is to erase it entirely, then place [REDACTED] or [DATA EXPUNGED] where it used to be. Alternatively, one can simply █████ ██████████ ████ ███ ████.

This line, I feel, is the most iconic piece of -j literature on the site. Absolutely astounding.

item.content:encoded:
This is like an amalgamation of all the memes about the SCP Foundation itself (and 173).

My favorite bits include:

  • Dr. Clef having the nick "Bright".
  • Speaking of Bright, having your place of employment constantly spam memes about you must be a bit weird.
  • The Foundation's Clearance system, one of its most defining traits, is based on the honor system.

I love it. +1

item.content:encoded:
I've upvoted for the chatroom and because I can't believe that one of my CaRenCon teammates was an O5!.

It made me chuckle.

Its funny how everyone in this discussion is masquerading as "users" on this "creative writing website." Way to keep character, everyone.

I too thought this was a bit clever. I can see how some may say that the ending log falls a bit flat, but that still doesn't change the fact that there are some hilarious moments. I'm not one to laugh at -J's, but I chuckled quite a bit throughout the article.

Joke SCPs are hard, and with this being an "001," the bar for voting is a bit askew. That being said, I think I can give this a +1 in terms of its short-form and making me chuckle

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don't particularly like this - it feels like a version of swann's proposal just without any subtlety. There's little here beyond "what if the roleplayers had a point" and it's such a basic premise that anyone who frequents chat could come up with if they base their ideation process on the things they see around then, which is a method I've always spoken out against.

But you had me at "We've been using the Wikidot domain for years!", and my vote for -Js is based on whether or not I laughed, so it's a +1 from me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I found a lot of the punchlines in this article fell flat. I did admittedly get some amusement out of this:

O5-1: Look, Two has a good point. Security is a bit lax. We don't need to constantly post Bright and SCP-173 memes to Reddit.

O5-8: But-

O5-1: I know, Eight. The peanut is funny.

But only because I recognize it — it's a massively common ironic community in-joke, and we bash it into the ground every single day on IRC and Discord. Come to think of it, most of the jokes here are in-jokes stated plainly, and then passed by just as plainly.

I'm not at all against seeing those types of in-jokes in articles; lampshading and showing self-awareness go a long way, and you certainly try both here. But I think you're still playing it too safe. A good chunk of your audience is already going to be inoculated against these jokes. To avoid speaking for others, and more for myself: I appreciate comedy when something new, something surprising or clever, something I've never considered before, is brought to the table and tested. Those things resonate with me. And I'm not getting them here. I recognize this is subjective, but remember, this is a Joke 001 Proposal. You've been granted express permission to go all out. Bring out the big guns, travel to places unseen.

item.content:encoded: Agreeing with barredowl: I had a good chuckle from the concept as well as the relatable encounters as written in the chat log about random users screaming "iS SCp REel!?", but I think it could've been taken to its full potential to make it even "better", in a way. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The chat logs, especially the codename gag with Bright, made me chuckle, but I can't help but feel the last log plays the concept too straight. Establishing that the SCP wiki is the product of the real SCP Foundation is a neat concept, but this article doesn't really take that to its full potential, instead making some surface-level jokes about what that would mean, and sorta just… dropping it early. The second half of the log exemplifies this — the punchline about masquerading as a creative writing site is kinda expected given everything else in the article, and fizzles out pretty quickly. It doesn't give that good of a final impression for me and sorta feels limp as an ending.

Still upvoting, because I enjoyed a majority of the jokes here, but I think this can be revised a bit further so that this article sticks the landing.
